Joel especially predicts Christ’s advent, 89. Christ’s first advent was like the whisper of a gentle breeze, 11. This peaceful advent breaks bow and sword, 22. Both advents of the Lord were for condemnation to the Jews, 142. The first is signified by the lion, the second by the bear, 142. God threatens those who hinder Christ’s advent, 232. The saints desire the second, 267. It is the building of God’s house, 304. The ancient Fathers built Christ’s advent as though building a house; and we build it whenever we read the book of Christ’s generation, 305. It was delayed because of original and actual sin, 386. The wall of enmity delayed Christ’s advent, 386. Christ’s two advents are signified by the striking of wings, one against the other, 691. Ephraim is called the adversary of truth, 86. There are three kinds of adversaries of faith, 294. The adversaries of the Church are Jews, heretics, and pagans, 294. Egypt. To invoke Egypt, turn toward Egypt, and return to Egypt differ, and are successive increases of sin, 58. It signifies the world from which God calls his own, 577. It is spiritual hell, 578. [Col. 1637] An enigma is an obscure proposition which is not easily understood unless it is explained, 270. The mystery of the woman with the issue of blood together with the ruler of the synagogue’s daughter, 636. Affliction of spirit, 487. The field of blood is Christ’s Church, 674. Persecutors of the Gospel are called agitators, 244. The paschal lamb was the Church’s first refreshment; hence the Church is called the “lintel of feasting,” 351. The farmer’s office belongs to God, 355. Wings signify pride, 34. Alexandria in Egypt was formerly called No, 252. Comparison of Alexandria and Nineveh, 252. Sinners are strangers to the heavenly Jerusalem, 108. The altar is Christ’s cross, 157. To walk in the name of one’s God is always to possess him, 209. Christ is called a friend, 273. Job’s friends had a good intention, 432. They nevertheless bear the appearance of heretics, 435. Amminadab is called Christ because he is king and priest, 417. Brotherly love, 534. Perverse love is to love reward while despising God, 58. It makes us like the things we love, 62. God’s love for the good is shown through the likeness of fruits, 62. It was a sign of love to send prophets to the Jews, and Christ himself, 364. God’s love causes those speaking of God not to err, 399. God’s love toward us is shown by the assumption of human nature, 697. The Amorite signifies the devil, 124. What spiritual impressment is, 610. Holy angels are called sons of God, 430. They are also called kings, 432. They bear the world, 444. Why the angel appeared in dreams to Joseph and the Magi, rather than openly, 576. Angels minister to the saints, 576. The angel fell from heaven not from virtue into vice, but from vice into vice, 696. Angel and human being fell from vice into vice, 696. The office of angels is to be sent to particular persons, 648. Angels appeared to the Fathers at Christ’s birth, passion, and resurrection, 695. Angel signifies the most high God, 290. Angel signifies faith, 345. Soul is used for life, 432. The soul is created by God, 561. Although adulterous, if betrothed to God through faith, it is a virgin, 22, 23. It is like a bird, and the word of God like a snare, 128. The soul’s beauty is to possess the knowledge of God, 141. The sinful soul is called a city of blood, 250. The soul is called queen when it seeks nothing earthly, but concubine when it serves under fear, 415. The soul which does not attain fear is called a young girl, 415. By hearing and keeping the Word of God, it becomes Jesus’ mother, 564. A fevered soul is one that labors under some sin at peril of life, 628. The grief of the soul on pilgrimage, 487. The living creatures among whom Christ was known were the two thieves—that is, the Church from Jews and Gentiles, that is, the two Testaments, 276. The living creatures that return and do not return: what they are, 697. How God is said to restore years to us, 101. The character of Antichrist, 453. His curse, 457. His last times, 474. Antichrist reproved, 514. Description of him, 514. His power, 514. The ancient Fathers are signified by she-goats and stags, 385. The boar from the wood signifies Titus and Vespasian, 274. The apostles are heavens, 24. Apostles and prophets were taught by God, 7. Apostolic men are vine-dressers, 20. By preaching to the Gentiles they opened the hope of victory, 20. Through the apostles’ preaching the earth received the seed of God, 24. Figure of the apostles’ flight and persecution, 47. The apostles were beautiful, strong, and pure in faith, 86. The progress and succession of the apostles’ preaching, 86. The apostles are the mountains of the heavenly Jerusalem, 109. The apostles are the bundle which Christ bound with the bond of charity on the day of Pentecost, and upon which he founded the Church, 161. They reaped what the patriarchs sowed, 161. By the grace of the Holy Spirit they inherited the Jews’ birthright as another Jacob, 172. They are called Saviors, 173. They are helmsmen of the ship, 179. They are gentle and severe, 216. Apostolic teaching is signified by dew, 215. The apostles are the Lord’s strong men: weak in flesh but strong in spirit, 245. They are reapers and treading-workers, 121. They are the Church’s teeth, 270. They are signified by the two men carrying the cluster on a pole, 327. They are Jacob’s remnant, 215. Apostles and martyrs are signified by the chariot of red horses, 330. They are like the horns of the altar, 343. The apostles, apostolic men, and doctors desire that the Church’s children not fail in tribulations, 352. They are the Lord’s feet, 357. Apostles, apostolic men, and teachers are signified by cedars, 382. What the apostles’ drunkenness was, 404. Why the apostles are compared to new wineskins, 636. They are the stones of which Joshua 4 speaks, 588. They were made ministers of reconciliation, 599. Why Christ chose poor apostles, [Col. 1638] 595. The apostles among the Jews were lightning, and lamps amid smoke, 600. Their names and their interpretation are given, 638. The apostles were ordained priests after Christ’s passion and resurrection, 638. Why the use of the sword was forbidden to the apostles, 596. Apostles and prophets are those whose Scripture may not be doubted, 662. Why apostles were called rams, 676. The waters of the sea signify teachers from among the Gentiles, 138. Waters signify an abundance of riches, 247. That human beings should be baptized in water was God’s counsel, 587. Lack of water caused the people to tempt the Lord twice, 592. Spiders’ webs: lies are compared to them because of their weakness, 54. The ark and winepress signify the afflictions of the saints, 101. Arcturus signifies the Church or the ancient Fathers, 127. To break bow, sword, and war is to be freed from the warfare of vices, 22. Israel’s bow is the carnal confidence of Judaism, 11. The winepress signifies charity, 345. It signifies the final judgment, 180. Silver signifies divine sayings, 472. Christ is called a ram, 676. Christ caught among brambles is among the blasphemies of the Jews, 383. Arrogance is a grave vice, 485. To ascend into heaven is to be raised by pride, 158. The ascension of saints into heaven is the building up of the body, 159. Whoever denies the ascension, resurrection, and judgment greatly detracts from God, 201. To climb the palm tree and to ascend the cross, 421. Christ’s ascension was prefigured by ascent onto the mountain, 597. To sprinkle seven times with the finger is for Christ’s passion to give us the sevenfold Spirit, 678. Assyria stands for all nations, 227. Avarice is the god of the Jews, 67. Avarice and lust are insatiable, 32. It is the cause of evils, 153. To have avarice in the head is to have it in the supreme intention of all things, 157. Roman avarice is criticized, 95. Jewish avarice is noted, 157. Jewish avarice stirred them to crucify Christ, 157. It is signified by fire, 222. It was evil to trade in the Temple and to sell Christ, 271. The avaricious person who gathers riches acquires shame for his house, 271. The avaricious person is always needy, 537. To hear a hearing is to hear with body and mind, 275. Hearing concerning the Incarnate Word is awe-inspiring, 275. A bird is so called from *aviditas* (“eagerness”), or because it travels through trackless places, 263. What it means to fly away like birds, 76. Ears hear not only the letter but also the spirit, 419. The Lord’s gold and silver are Holy Scripture, 107. Gold was the Jews’ god, 157. Gold signifies the inner sense of Scripture, silver the outer, 381. It is Christ’s divinity, 410. By gold is denoted the life of the righteous, 524. The south wind is the Holy Spirit, 402.

### B

Baal: Jezebel brought this idol from Sidon, and Israel worshipped it, 53. Baals are any idols whatever, 19, 22. Baptism. The sons of Baptism are called sons of the sea, 75. One enlivened by sacred baptism is like a bird flying out of Egypt, 76. It is a sea, 100, 346. Christ’s baptism was the beginning of his preaching and of Jewish envy, 280. It destroys pride and makes people humble, 340. It is the fountain of the house of David, 352. It makes saints of those who had previously been kids, 382. Christ’s baptism at the beginning of his preaching was prefigured by Aaron’s washing at the beginning of his consecration, 589. His baptism in water was for our humility, 587. It was established in Christ’s death, and after his resurrection and ascension, 638. That people should be baptized in water was God’s counsel, 587. Why Christ wished to be baptized in the Jordan rather than in other waters, 588. What baptism in the Holy Spirit and fire is, 590. Golden bases signify God’s counsel and inflexibility in judgment, 412. Eight woes correspond to the eight beatitudes, 125. Wherein the blessedness of the ancient Fathers consists, 698. Blessed is the one whom God teaches, 7. Mary is called blessed and beautiful because of faith, 388. The blessed both see and await God, 698. What the state of the blessed is like, 698. No one is certain concerning it, 445. To sanctify war is to baptize, 107. To bless is sometimes used for to curse, 430. How Saint Benedict the abbot saw the whole world gathered together, 593. God recalls benefits bestowed upon the wicked in order to rebuke their ingratitude, 61. When the people received greater gifts from God, they then withdrew from him, 221. Benefits given to saints by God are ointments by which others come to him, 377. [Col. 1639] Beasts obey the saints, 22. Beasts of the earth are malign spirits, 438, 511. Beth-aven was the place where Jeroboam set one calf, 33. Beth-peor is the same as Priapus, the god of the Romans, 62. The number two is a symbol of marriage, 26. It also signifies nuptials, 425. The Jews’ blasphemies are thorns, 383. The Law promised earthly goods, but the Gospel eternal goods, 43. The good are to be preferred to the bad, 8. They are the reason why God does good to the bad on their account, 12. Good and bad are mixed in the Church, 17. The good are fruits, but the bad leaves, 153. Temporal goods are like fruits that soothe children, and are of little worth, 153. Good works follow the dying person, 243. Ox. In Palestine, they say, oxen and other animals bring forth crops, 69. Oxen are called God’s workers, producing fruit, 148. Oxen signify good laborers, 431. The ox also signifies the Jewish people, 439. It signifies the Synagogue, 439. Wild oxen are proud Jews, 148.

### C
Great blindness is unwillingness to understand the law of God, 55. **Heaven.** To ascend into heaven is to be lifted up on the wings of pride, 158. No one can enter except through Christ, 300. Why the Lord did not accept Cain’s offerings, 363. Caiaphas’s prophecy was bloodstained, 205. The shoes of body and spirit differ, 418. The devil does not attack those shod with the spirit, 418. A slanderer says only those things that can arouse envy; the rest he keeps silent, 152. Channels are the counsels of the Divinity, 421. The latticework signifies the first patriarchs, Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob, 386. The golden lampstand signifies Christ crowned with glory because of the Passion, 323. We call those books and prophecies canonical which we received from the Jews, not from the gentiles, 102. A song is perfect when its octave is the same as its first note, 414. The notable songs of the Old Testament are seven, 373. The male and female singers of the Old Testament, 524. Hairs signify the most subtle thoughts, 394. Goats and stags signify the ancient Fathers, 385. The captivities of Judah and Israel are signified by spirit, agitation, and fire; and how many years those captivities lasted, 11. The captivity of the ten tribes has not been dissolved, but they remained among the Persians, 12, 25. Our captivity began with the sin of the first human being, 104. The captives of Jerusalem during Titus’s siege numbered 96,000, while those killed numbered 1,100,000, 357. There are two mountains of Carmel, 122.

**Flesh.** The desires of the flesh are called the beasts of the earth, 437. The flesh fights against the Spirit, 537. God does not regard the stock of the flesh, but the dispositions of the soul, 106. Against the flesh and lust, help must be sought from God, 344. Flesh and blood signify sins, 203. To mortify the flesh is to let myrrh drip from one’s hands, 407. Christ’s flesh is an ivory womb, which shone with divine privileges, 412; it is purer than the rest, 412. To chastise the pride of kings is done not with lions and bears, but with frogs and flies, 101. One who is to be punished as an example to others ought to be known and placed on high, 266. The virtue of chastity is commended, 481. The well-guarded seal of chastity is signified by the female joint, 418. Perfect chastity consists in being chaste not only in deed but also in affection, 418. God’s case against human beings is just, but the human case against God is unjust, 220. Cedars signify the apostles, teachers of the Church, and prelates, 282. The number one hundred signifies perfection, 136. The number one hundred is a square number, 539. The number one hundred is used for infinity, 467. Charity is signified by the battle bow, 345. It makes another’s good its own, 345.

Christ is signified by Gideon, 72. Christ’s triumph is like Gideon’s triumph, 72. Christ is signified by Hosea, 67. Christ’s Passion is figured and extensively explained, 45, 46. Christ is like dew in the Virgin’s womb, 46, 86. He is the Doctor of righteousness, 99. Christ’s killers are signified by the summit of Carmel, 113. Against them a terrible sentence is pronounced, 113. He is proved to be God, 134. On the cross the Lord stands above the altar, 157. He is the legate sent to the nations, 165. He is called Hebrew, that is, “one who crosses over,” 178. He is questioned about everything about which Jonah is questioned, 178. He restored God’s likeness in the human being, 181. He is mountain, house, and foundation, 207. Christ’s holiness is greater than that of all the saints [Col. 1640], 207. Christ’s body is called a temple, 303. Christ is a heap of twenty measures—that is, God and human being—whereas the Jews made him a heap of ten measures, that is, believed him to be merely human, 307. He is signified by Zerubbabel, 309. In the Passion and in other matters he precedes the martyrs and all the saints, 312. He is called the servant of the Lord, 321. He is less than the angels, 321. He has nothing sinister; everything in him is on the right, 321. He is a brand plucked from the fire, 321. He is the stone upon which were seven eyes, that is, the seven gifts of the Spirit, 322. He is signified by the golden lampstand, 322. When Christ was born, one must not fight with natural but with spiritual weapons, 323. Christ’s glory after the resurrection is greater than before it, 324. Christ is crowned in his elect, 323. He is king and priest, and alone sits upon his throne, 417. Christ prophesied about himself beyond all the prophets, 355. He is a farmer, 355. He is called the male among the flock, 366. He is called a lily because, although his humanity is pure, his divinity within is nevertheless incomparable, 383. He is called a lily among thorns because he endured blasphemies from the Jews, 383. He is a rock and a wall, 387. He is a vineyard, 388. How he is to be sought, 390. He is a purple ascent, 393. He is to be seen and known from the sayings of the prophets, 393. Coming into the world, he did four principal things, 402. White in holiness and red in the Passion, 410. Christ’s divinity is gold, 411. Christ came to call sinners to repentance, 411. He is called Aminadab because he is king and priest, 417. He was incarnate, suffered, rose again, and ascended into heaven willingly, 417. He is our brother on his mother’s side, 422. Christ is God, human being, king, and priest, 565. He is known through his incarnation, Passion, resurrection, and ascension, 565. He is truly human, 565. He is greater than the angels; and his lesser status is figured by the angels ascending and descending on Jacob’s ladder, 568. He could not have been manifested better in any way than by preaching repentance, 582. Christ’s strength shows him to be God, 585. To follow Christ and take up the cross is great strength, 644. Why Christ commanded his followers not to tell anyone who he was, 646. No other Christ is to be expected, 647. He is the lesser one in the kingdom of heaven, 649. He is called a child, 649. He alone was bought by the Jews, and they killed him, 660. He is priest and victim in different respects, 676. Christ’s arrest on the night of the Passover was figured in the wickedness of the Sodomites against Lot, 45. Christ died in the thirty-third year of his age, 276. Christ is signified by Job, 428, 430. He continually sacrifices for us, 430. He is likewise called light, 433. The balance, 439, 481. He is mediator between God and human beings, 481. His death is called the shadow of death, 434. In the person of Job he laments his own affliction, 458. His wisdom is proclaimed, 472. Christ is compared with a mustard seed, 473. His humility, 483. He alone is wise, 525.

We Christians rest in the Law and the Prophets, which were the Jews’ cord, 292. We Christians are children of martyrs and saints, 346. Christians should learn both to praise God and to fight against the devil, 414. A Christian must not entangle himself in Pharisaic traditions, 635. Three orders of Christians are established, 677. The true food of those who follow God is the word of God, 82. The food of the saints is the praise of God, 102. To go around cities and villages is to preach the Gospel, 390. Circumcision of the heart is perfect love of God, 420. The best city of refuge is to forgive one’s brother, 616. The city of the Lord is the Church, 633. To cry out to God is to desire him; whoever does not do this howls, 49. Those who cry out to the Lord he always hears, 99. Christ and the saints cry out to God, but in different ways, 183. Christ cries out in the prophets, 260. To limp, when our foot or our faith is mentioned, 210. God’s clemency is shown, 75. Uniformity of thoughts is uniformity of face and one eye, 397. Subtle thoughts are hairs, 394. Thoughts are signified by Job’s camels, 429; they are likewise signified by his household, 430. The Jews hindered knowledge of the incarnation, Passion, and so forth, 417. To worship idols is to celebrate and venerate them by one’s own will, 66. An outstretched neck signifies pride; an unoutstretched one, Mary’s humility, 419. Seven properties of the dove are attributed to Mary, 394. The dove signifies works of piety, 596. To eat the sins of the people is to keep the people in sin for the sake of profit, 31. A procession returning from a feast is the rite of Jewish ceremonies, 387. The comparison of unbelievers with Christians, and what their righteousness ought to be [Col. 1641], 237. Contrition is twofold, 419. Mary’s conception from the Holy Spirit is signified by dew lying in the wilderness, and is wondrous, 572. Preachers are called kings, 434; they are likewise stars, 444. Their encomium, 502. They are compared with horses, 508. Concubines are imperfect souls, and the number eight is attributed to them for a reason, 415. Praise of concord, 534. Desire, which gives birth to sin, is signified by the liver, 82. Not to touch another’s property out of desire is to sit beneath one’s own vine, 209. Confession of sins, 446. It does not exist where truth does not exist, 29. Christ’s confession about himself is the greatest of all, 654. Christ’s confession that he is the Son of God is praiseworthy, 653. Judas’s confession was like the confession of demons, 672. The person confessing should acknowledge his sin like Lamech, 363. Let our confidence be in God, 85, 423. It arises either from love or from pride, 630. Humility is called brokenness, 83. The devil gathers sinners like sand, 265. Carnal and spiritual marriage exist no less than marriage between two persons, 22. Holy marriage, such as that of Mary and Joseph, exists where there is one faith and one spirit, 568. Divine counsel is signified by golden vessels, 412. Divine counsels are channels, 422. The Lord sends as many consolations as curses, 171. The Lord consoles the good in two ways, just as he afflicts the wicked in two ways, 239. For Christ’s servants, it is to suffer as he suffered, 642. Constantine’s donation to the Roman pontiff is mentioned, 187. Habit makes one love what would otherwise be laborious, 69. The contemplative person is like Jacob, for he sleeps and is wakeful in his mouth, 406. Contrition properly belongs to children, and they properly stand in tribulation, 83. It is twofold, bodily and spiritual, 85. Great contrition or compunction is signified by Heshbon, 419. True conversion to God consists first in changing the heart through repentance, 96. To convert a sinner is to bite the wicked one, that is, the devil, 270. The sinner’s good conversion is to recognize his sin and confess God to be just, 312. Those who are converted are the glory of those through whom they are converted, 323. Feasts incite sinners to kill the saints, 237. The many evils of feasts, 237. The feast of Job’s sons, 428. Softening the heart for repentance is dissolving it, 278. The hardness of the heart is softened through humility, 281. “One heart” is called the number one, but our heart here is divided, 298. The impenitent person is said to dwell in the land of the North, 317. It is compared with adamant because of its hardness, 334. The heart and arm of the beloved are the holy Scriptures, 423. The heart of women is on the right side, 555. The horns of the altar signify the strength of the apostles, 344. For Christ to have horns in his hands is for all power to be given him and for him to draw everything to himself, 278. The crown of precious stone on Christ’s head is Scripture illuminated by testimonies of miracles, 629. Christ is crowned in his elect, 332. What Chorazin, Bethsaida, and Capernaum signify mystically, 651. We must believe that the body is truly present in the sacrament of the altar, because God says so, 383. He granted us remission of sins differently from the ancients, 663. How he restored the ancient dead before his Passion, and how he restores us, 664. The sacrament of the body and blood was a great temptation for some, 664. The human body was made by God, not Satan, against the Manichaeans, 446. Correction is useful, 542. Drunkenness is not always spoken of as evil, 351. “The following day” sometimes signifies an uncertain time, but sometimes the next day, 622. It is accursed and opposed to the present day, 622. A creature serving the uses of sinners is called captive, 18. Even an insensible creature obeys the divine voice, 347. What the devil’s creation by God was like, 266. To believe Christ to be God and human being is to ascend, by which we are admitted to refreshment and understanding of the Scriptures, 392. The two legs of the Bridegroom are mercy and truth, 412. Christ’s cross is an altar, 157. The tree of the cross brought the fruit of salvation and life, 423. To take up the cross is the greatest strength, 644. Christ’s cross is the tribunal of the dreadful Judge, 675. Four persons stood around the cross, 675. How the crucified human being was properly forsaken, 96. Desire is a prostitute who makes us fornicate away from God, 251. Christ healed Jews and gentiles in different ways, 627 [Col. 1642]. To guard vanity is to love it, 182. The guardians of the vineyard are the patriarchs and prophets, 225. The guardians of the house are called stars or angels, 560.

## D

Demons are denoted by the Sabaeans, 431. Demons are called foxes because of their malice, and birds because of their pride, 630. They are like horsemen among the Romans and among tyrants, 262. Damascus, a city, is the place where Cain killed Abel, 113. Daniel, being pure in heart, deserved to see God, 599. David’s humility is commended, 381. David saw, with the same eyes as Moses, the plans of the Temple built by Solomon, 413. He was a figure of Christ and had four faces—that of a man, lion, calf, and so forth, 671. Debts owed to us by right are not debts we are obliged to forgive, 615. The tithe signifies the sanctification of righteousness, 126. Jacob was the first to offer tithes, 126. The number ten is perfect, 126. Tithing is called election, and the tenth is called the elect, 339. Shrines signify Jewish superstitions, 56. The teeth of the Church are the apostles and preachers, 270. Teeth signify those who bite and slanderers, 395. Mary’s teeth, however, are her innocence, 395. How Christ was properly forsaken on the cross, 96. He descends who humbly confesses, 77. To descend into hell is to despair, 158. Let a person descend willingly, lest he descend unwillingly, 588. The desert is every soul which, having abandoned God, is abandoned by him, 61. It is whatever lies outside the Church of God, 295. Such persons are called contemptible in the Church, 358. A soul may be deserted even among crowds, 391. Jerusalem is called a desert, 677. The bridegroom’s desire is to love, ask for, or long for, 386. Desire, when delayed, is a punishment, 445. Jerusalem’s destruction by Titus was irreparable, 150. Slanderers do not reckon their own crimes, 448.

God is made known to us through his chief works, 81. To follow God according to his pastures is to follow him for temporal goods, 82. God is called the creator and founder of the elect, but the maker of the great wicked, 149. God’s beauty and wisdom are judged nonexistent by the weak, 235. God alone is unchangeable; the devil is changeable, 261. God the Father and his hidden judgments are signified by Mount Paran, 276. God does not change, but the qualities of the creatures with which he has dealings do, 383. God’s becoming human was an increase of his beauty, 282. He is our Father because he loved us when we were enemies, 612. In dying for human beings, he wisely did what he could so that they would not sin, 696. God is to be feared, 554. God must not be resisted, 443. He judges justly, 445. He converts the nations, 444, 501. In his eyes no one is clean, 446. Human sins are known to him, 446. His majesty and power, 448. He cannot be seen by a traveler, 465. He is to be feared, 465. His strength and wisdom, 450, 468. God’s providence, 532. God is not a respecter of persons, 490. His judgments are unsearchable, 494. He punishes the wicked, 491. Those who deny that God exists, 531. God’s wisdom is far removed from us, 546. How the book of Deuteronomy differs from the other books of the Law, 593. God has a right hand and no left, 321. The right hand signifies glory, 384. God’s right hand is the hope of eternal recompense; the left hand signifies temporal goods, 423.

The devil comes from the North and is the prince of our reproach, 99. He is signified by Asshur, 100, 296. How, having been expelled by Christ, he is punished, 100. Though dead, he lives in the wicked, 100. He begets more children for death than there are elect persons, 253. He gathers the wicked like sand, 264. He laughs at those whom he subjects to himself, 264. Since he has no God, he himself is called god by his own people, 264. He was judged in three ways, 265. The devil’s strength is empty and deceptive, 265. The devil is the head of the wicked, 281. He is called falsehood, 350. How the devil rose against God’s servants with God’s permission, 401. In Christ’s incarnation, a human being is the head, 569. He made himself the author of the human race because he corrupted it, 692. The devil’s purpose was that the creature should be unable to know the Creator, 692. The devil was vain and the prince of vanity, 692. Rebuke of the devil, 511. The devil stood with the angels, 429. He accuses blessed Job, 429. Demons are signified by the Chaldeans, 431. Satan slanders blessed Job, 431. He asks God for the power to afflict him, 432. He is an exactor, 435. He is represented by the lion, 436. He is armed, 437. He is humbled by God, 510. The diadem with which Christ was crowned is the ancient Church of the patriarchs and prophets, together with their sayings, 393. What kind of symphony the diapason is, 414. *Diapsalma*, that is, *sela*, is a marking of musical sound and denotes perpetuity, 277. What kind of symphony the diatessaron is, 415. The day of Christ’s Passion and resurrection, by which we were freed from the devil’s bondage, is most celebrated, 13. The day of sinners and evil persons is when they withdraw from God, 45. Why it is called the Lord’s day, 94. How Christ was in the tomb for three days and nights, 180. The day of tribulation for the righteous has seven names, 169. “Day” is understood as the whole period of this world’s life, 244. The day of cold is the day of tribulation and adversity, 255. Day signifies the time of grace, 352. The day of resurrection is called “day,” 358. Distrust is called fear, 101. Perverse love is loving the reward while despising God, 58. A sign of love was the sending of prophets to the Jews and of Christ himself, 366. Love makes another’s good our own, 393. Love and rivalry are lamps of fire and flames, and make one rage, 424. Great love is love of the Word, 424. Love of enemies was introduced only with the law of grace, because it was impossible under the old law, 610. Love of enemies distinguishes the children of God from the children of the devil, 611. It is the root of good works, 611. To love mercy is to seek mercy diligently, 221.
